title: Constrain safe midpoint arithmetic
prompt: midpoint accepts one integral type except bool, following std::midpoint: return the middle value rounded toward the first argument for odd distances. It must avoid signed overflow, even at int limits.
signature: template<std::integral T> T midpoint(T a,T b) except bool

tests.label: Ordinary midpoint
tests.hint: An odd distance rounds toward the first value.

tests.label: Reverse rounding
tests.hint: Changing argument order can change the rounded side.

tests.label: Across zero
tests.hint: Do not compute an overflowing sum.

hints: std::integral is a C++20 concept checked during compilation.
std::midpoint handles endpoints without first adding them.
explanation: The requires clause excludes bool at compile time; std::midpoint performs overflow-safe arithmetic for accepted integer types. No runtime error handling is needed for an invalid type.
